claim or remark: the paper's bold 'Observation' asserts that U_j is a multi-frequency CZ operator without proof; made a semi_formal claim because Proposition 4.1 is built on it.
The only argument for Theorem 0.1 is one sentence opening Section 2 (weak L^1 bound, then interpolation and duality); it is a prose proof node, and Theorem 0.1 is marked semi_formal.

Theorem 0.2 (s in (1,p)) is proved in the paper only for s>=2, as Corollary 3.3; the general case is left to Propositions 3.1 and 3.2. Theorem 0.2 is semi_formal, with a specializes edge to CP1 and uses edges from PrP2 and PrP3.
The parser flagged only 4 of the 6 \\item properties of the decomposition in the proof of Proposition 2.1 as labels. All six items were made steps so that the list is segmented uniformly.
A sentence separates the proof of Proposition 3.1 from its statement, so the parser gave no proves target. The proves edge to PrP2 was added by hand.
The closing 'Question' runs into an itemize. The open problem spans the whole list, and the cited unit-ball Bochner-Riesz bound (Lee; Tao) inside its second item is nested as an external theorem.

Left out: the introduction's first statement of the multi-frequency Hilbert transform symbol and its optimality comment after Theorem 0.1 (the Section 1.1 copy and Remark 2.1 were kept); the class W^p(p_0,q_0), which is never used again; motivational sentences.

\label{thm:boundedness} Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies and $T$ an associated multi-frequency Calder\'on-Zygmund operator. Then 
\begin{itemize}
 \item for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $T$ is bounded on $L^p$ with
$$ \|T\|_{L^p \to L^p} \lesssim N^{\left|\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{2}\right|}.$$
 \item for $p=1$, $T$ is of weak-type $(1,1)$ with
$$ \|T\|_{L^1 \to L^{1,\infty}} \lesssim N^{\frac{1}{2}}.$$
\end{itemize}

\label{def:max} Let $\Theta$ be a collection of $N$ frequencies and $s\in[1,\infty)$. Consider a ball $Q$, we denote by ${\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}$ the projection operator (in the $L^s$-sense) on the subspace of $L^s(3Q)$, spanned by $(\exp {i\xi\cdot})_{\xi\in \Theta}$. Let us specify this projection operator: consider $E$ the finite dimensional sub-space of $L^s(3Q)$, spanned by $(e^{i\xi\cdot})_{\xi\in \Theta}$ and equipped with the $L^s(3Q)$-norm.
Since $E$ is of finite dimension, then for every $f\in L^s(Q)$ there exists $v:={\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f)\in E$ such that
$$ \|f-v\|_{L^s(3Q)} = \inf_{\phi\in E} \|f-\phi\|_{L^s(3Q)}.$$
This projection operator may depend on $s$, which is not important for our purpose so this is implicit in the notation and we forget it.

\medskip\noindent
Since $0\in E$, we obviously have 
\begin{equation} \label{eq:projection}\|{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f)\|_{L^s(3Q)} \leq 2\|f\|_{L^s(Q)}. \end{equation} Then, we may define the maximal sharp function 
$$ {\mathcal M}_{s,\Theta}^\sharp (f)(x_0) := \sup_{x_0\in Q} \left(\aver{Q} \left|f-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(f{\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s  dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.$$

We follow the well-known proof for usual Calder\'on-Zygmund operators and adapt the arguments to the current situation. So consider a point $x_0$ and a ball $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $x_0$, we have to estimate
$$ \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.$$
We split the function into a local part $f_0$ and an off-diagonal part $f_\infty$: 
$$f=f_0+f_\infty:= f{\bf 1}_{10 Q} + f {\bf 1}_{(10 Q)^c}.$$ 
By definition of the projection operator, we know that
\begin{align*}
 \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} & \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} \\
 & \leq \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_0) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} + \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_\infty)-{\mathbb P}_{\Theta,Q}(T(f_\infty){\bf 1}_Q) \right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}}.
\end{align*}
For the local part, we use boundedness in $L^s$ of the operator $T$ (Proposition \ref{prop:bound}), hence
\begin{align*}
 \left( \aver{Q} \left|T(f_0)\right|^s dx \right)^{\frac{1}{s}} & \lesssim |Q|^{-\frac{1}{s}} \|T(f_0)\|_{L^s(Q)} \lesssim  N^{(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s})} \left(|Q|^{-\frac{1}{s}} \|f_0\|_{L^s}\right) \\
& \lesssim N^{|\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{s}|} {\mathcal M}_s(f)(x_0).
\end{align*}
Then let us focus on the second part, involving $f_\infty$. \\
We use the decomposition (with an integral representation) since we are in the off-diagonal case: for $x\in Q$ 
$$ T(f_\infty)(x) = \sum_{j=1}^N  \int K_j(x,y) f_\infty(y) dy.$$
Consider the following function, defined on $3Q$ by (where $c(Q)$ is the center of $Q$)
$$ \Phi:=  x\in 3Q \rightarrow \sum_{j=1}^N  \int  e^{i\xi_j\cdot (x-c(Q))} K_j(c(Q),y) f_\infty(y) dy.$$

\end{align*}

$$ \|\sigma_j\|_{L^2} \lesssim |\{\xi, d(\xi,\partial \Omega)\simeq 2^j \}|^{\frac{1}{2}} \lesssim 2^{\frac{j}{2}}.$$
